simple.meaning: אַכְזָר (ʼakzâr) is a Hebrew word meaning “violent ; by implication deadly ; also (in a good sense) brave.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַכְזָר (H393) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:33, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Job, Lamentations.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַכְזָר (H393) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַכְזָר (H393) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַכְזָר (ʼakzâr) / H393 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:33, Job 30:21, Job 41:2, Lamentations 4:3 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: violent ; by implication deadly ; also (in a good sense) brave
definitions.full: H393. akzar אַכְזָר adjective cruel, fierce , of poison ( ראֹשׁ ) Deut 32:33 ; elsewhere of men, fierce Job 41:2 ; as substantive = a cruel one 30:21 (of God), Lam 4:3 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (apparently meaning to act harshly);

occurrences.englishText: Their wine is the poison of serpents,
You have turned to be cruel to me.
Can you put a rope into his nose,
Even the jackals offer their breast.
